findings.evidence: scratch probe printed admission_order ['crit','review','lower'] vs fair_share ['lower','crit','review']
findings.summary: priorities_first excludes the critical request from `raised` but still prepends every other hoisted override to `rest`, where the critical request sits at index 0 because it is neither a review nor aged, so the lead scan stops immediately; result: with a critical (=100) and a lower override (=10) queued beside a review, fair_share_admission_order returns [lower, crit, review], so the lower-priority request takes the freed slot and the critical request waits.
findings.text: Reproduced against e04648c6 in a scratch extraction: fair_share_admission_order([review, crit@100, lower@10]) -> ['lower','crit','review'], while admission_order gives the correct ['crit','review','lower']. This is the production admission path (admission/selection.py:393).
findings.title: a sub-critical override is hoisted ahead of a critical request

findings.summary: fair_queue_order_details is called without config_for, so the project's retuned queue.critical_priority is ignored and the shipped default 100 applies there; a project that sets 50 gets 50 only in admission, not in promotion ordering.
findings.text: The optional config_for added to fair_queue_order_details defaults to None at its only external call site, so _critical_level always reads the shipped default 100 on that path.
findings.title: project critical level not threaded into the promotion-requests ordering

findings.summary: Two dict-comprehension reflows in validate_layer and unknown_key_paths are unrelated to critical priority; harmless but out-of-goal churn inside a declared path.
findings.text: flight.py:1826 and flight.py:2002 collapse multi-line comprehensions to one line; neither relates to the critical level.
findings.title: unrelated formatting reflows in flight.py

verdicts.done_when: done_when names tests/test_a_critical_request_takes_a_slot_before_reviews.py; the override-100/99/none and project-level-50 cases plus the shipped-defaults strict-resolution test all pass in after_suite (64 passed, EXIT=0), 0 added failures vs baseline (59 passed).
verdicts.goal: The node goal is a critical override takes a freed slot ahead of a delivered run's review; admission/ordering.py and queue_order.py add a (-1) critical class, but a sub-critical override is hoisted ahead of it in the fair-share path.
